results.title: Garv
results.overview: Garv's only trying to get ahead. Fresh into a new life in Melbourne, he's landed a decent job, a shot at succes, and a workplace that's anything but welcoming. As the cracks begin to show, a few harmless jokes turn into something harder to ignore. But when speaking up makes him the problem, Garv's forced to confront an uncomfortable truth; sometimes, fitting in comes at a cost.

results.title: The Tragic Tragedy of John Low
results.original_title: The Tragic Tragedy of John Low
results.overview: When struggling Director John Low is the first person to discover the low angle shot, he attempts to capitalise off of the idea by putting it under his own copyright.

results.title: #Vymara
results.overview: Four washed-up creators livestream their search for a missing YouTuber linked to a conspiracy and uncover a sinister truth never meant to go viral.

results.title: Treehugger
results.overview: In a land of damp mist, a wooden doll wanders, carrying a quiet longing for connection. There he meets a fragile young tree, equally awkward, equally alone. Neither knows how to hug. Yet, what begins as a tentative reaching out soon dissolves into a fever of desire—a slow descent into an attachment too heavy for such little souls.

results.title: Saturn or a Brief Treatise on Melancholy
results.original_title: Saturno o pequeño tratado de la melancolía
results.overview: In Lagunas del Rosario, in the arid lands of Mendoza, Rubén Díaz—artisan, Malvinas War veteran, and healer known as Caballo Loco (Crazy Horse)—each winter solstice summons a secret ceremony exclusively for initiates. During a night-long vigil, pilgrims from distant places gather in search of relief from illness, grief, and pain. Surrounded by bonfires, prayers, and ancestral stories, the community attempts to conjure away the afflictions of a territory ravaged by drought and the vanishing of its waters.

results.title: Unseen: The Aberfan Portraits
results.overview: Following the Aberfan disaster in 1966, an artist from Llandudno embarked on an extraordinary mission to paint portraits of most of the 116 children who lost their lives, using photographs and locks of hair provided by their grieving families.  For the first time, relatives share what these remarkable paintings have meant to them over the past six decades. Presented by the BBC’s Huw Thomas, he discovers how the portraits became enduring symbols of remembrance in a village touched by tragedy.

results.title: Aberfan: The Village That Fought Back
results.original_title: Aberfan: The Village That Fought Back
results.overview: Aberfan's grieving community takes on the government, demanding justice and removal of the remaining tips after the disaster that killed 144 people

results.title: The Final Embrace: 'Chi come me'
results.overview: This documentary explores the phenomenon behind Chi come me, a hit theatrical production directed by Andrée Ruth Shammah and written by Roy Chen. Following its final sold-out run at Milan's Teatro Franco Parenti, the film examines how a powerful story about five fragile teenagers in a mental health center finding their voice through theater transformed into an intergenerational cult experience and a profound mirror of contemporary adolescent struggles.

results.title: Posers
results.overview: Munro Logan And Emme Go To A Gig, The Gig  Afterwards Munro Realises His Friends Are Not Who They Claim To Be

results.title: Evening Light
results.overview: 6 October 2025. In the evening the impossible happened. A white horse walked into a prison, looked into the cells, came out into the light.

results.title: Somnambula
results.overview: From a dream a dancer is born — the living embodiment of thunder. His journey unfolds in the space between dream and reality, where movement releases a force of nature and the body becomes nature’s voice.

results.title: Memory: A Film that Tries to Remember Itself
results.original_title: Memory: A Film that Tries to Remember Itself
results.overview: Using visual data extracted from found 8mm footage, the film attempts to reconstruct itself—bit by bit, colour by colour, line by line. This process unfolds through data visualization, tracing how images are absorbed, fragmented and remembered.

results.title: Of Swallows
results.overview: A swallow’s eye is longer than other birds. Their visual acuity is said to resemble Raptors. For sailors, swallows are a good omen signifying a close shore. My father loved birds. Since his passing I've felt afloat. Lost and unanchored. At sea in overwhelming emotions. I close my eyes and look for swallows, as metaphorical groundings.

results.title: Standing Prayer II
results.overview: A film prayer. Giraffes gather in an enclosure to usher a mysterious ritual.

results.title: The Stream XV
results.overview: Time dwells within all that flows.  I live in the Ogura-ike Reclaimed Land in Kyoto.  Wind, water and lines of cars pass across this land.  On the highway, time moves straight toward the future.  Yet there are places where time flows backward—rivers, forests, shrines and villages, where time returns to its source.  The echo of wind chimes that rang here a hundred years ago still resonates today.

results.title: Lure
results.overview: As the sun starts to set in a secluded wood, an unwelcome guest emerges from the periphery, drawn into a glittering snare. Time slouches, voices murmur from between the trees and corrosion starts ahead of schedule. Be careful out there. You might catch your death.
